A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CADS/R1-SyntheticVL study. All pages are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite both referring to one in Section 4.2.

before.justification: v1 reports original R1-SyntheticVL evaluations, component ablations, synthetic-versus-real-data comparisons and data-scaling experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including R1-SyntheticVL's 75.6 MathVista score, component ablations and training-data comparisons.

M1.justification: CAD-Generate's three steps and four synthesis strategies, CAD-Judge's consensus filtering, adversarial context optimization and GRPO training remain unchanged. The added reward description documents implementation details without establishing a revised training objective.

E1.justification: Both use MMSynthetic-20K, MM-Eureka samples for the real-data comparison, and the same six evaluation benchmarks: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision, MMMU, MMMU-Pro and CharXiv. The added healthcare citations do not introduce healthcare experiments.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same generator comparisons, Table 2 retains the same general and reasoning MLLMs, and Table 4 retains the real-data comparator. OpenVLThinker's citation changes from Deng et al., 2025 to 2026, but its comparator identity and reported scores remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated base model, existing training settings, evaluation columns, scaling sample sizes and 2K-per-source real-versus-synthetic comparison remain unchanged. v2 discloses additional KL, sampling and reward details without revising a previously stated setting or introducing a new experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, real-data comparison and mixing analysis in Table 4, scaling experiment in Figure 3 and qualitative examples in Figure 4 are retained. No new robustness, sensitivity or error analysis is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random-seed identifiers, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain all result entries and values, and Figure 3 retains the same scaling curve. For example, R1-SyntheticVL remains at 75.6 on MathVista and 52.0 average in Table 2; Table 4 retains 72.2, 73.3 and 74.6. Qualitative examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), including the consensus score and adversarial-instance condition 1 ≤ C < K, are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty and effectiveness claims for CADS, MMSynthetic-20K and R1-SyntheticVL. No core contribution or benchmark-performance claim is added, removed or substantively revised.

C2.justification: v2 adds an Impact Statement explicitly interpreting CADS as improving data-acquisition cost efficiency, scalability and resource efficiency through reduced dependence on manual collection and annotation. These benefits are not quantified. The expanded scaling discussion otherwise preserves v1's interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies a KL penalty coefficient of 1e-2, top p = 1, top k = -1, and a reward combining accuracy and format components. v1 omitted these details. Hardware, existing hyperparameters and the future code/model/data release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1 and 2.1 add five cited works: He et al., 2025; Jin et al., 2026; Lan et al., 2022; Ma et al., 2026; and Yao et al., 2026, covering healthcare, cardiac signals and multimodal search. The central positioning against earlier synthesis approaches remains unchanged; several existing references also receive bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 corrects scattered grammar and spelling errors, lightly rewrites the motivation and scaling discussion, and updates affiliation and publication information. It adds Impact Statement and Acknowledgment sections before the references while retaining the main section sequence and narrative.

P2.justification: The same four figures and four tables remain with unchanged numbering and substantive content. Figures are slightly resized, Table 4 moves directly beneath Figure 3 on page 7, Figure 1's caption receives a small edit, and first-page and reference layouts change.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional reproducibility information through the newly specified KL, sampling and reward settings in Section 4.1, and improves readability through copyediting. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged. The new Impact Statement's efficiency claims remain unquantified, so the overall gain is limited to clearer and more complete documentation.
